name: Sewing Machine Hospital
character: Machines on IV drips: patient, practical repair craft for the machines our quilts depend on.

sections.title: Every machine deserves a checkup
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Tune-ups, repairs, and vintage restorations for the machines our quilts depend on, usually back on your table within a week.

items.title: Annual tune-up
items.body: Clean, oil, tension, timing check, and a sew-off on three fabrics.

items.title: Repair diagnosis
items.body: Applied to the repair if you approve it the same day.

items.title: Vintage restoration
items.body: Belts, wiring, motors, and cabinets for the machines worth saving.

items.title: Trade-in credit
items.body: Working machines taken on credit toward service or a refurbished one.

sections.heading: On the bench
sections.html:
Most of what walks in is thread soup in the bobbin area and a needle installed backwards. Both are a ten-minute fix and we will show you how so the next one is yours to fix.

The rest is timing, feed dogs, and motors that ran out of carbon brushes around the second Nixon administration. We keep those parts on the shelf, not on order.

items.quote: My 1974 Singer came home running quieter than the day my mother bought it.
items.author: R., Fairborn

items.quote: They found the fault in twenty minutes after another shop had my machine for six weeks.
items.author: T., Oakwood

sections.title: Services and pricing
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Flat rates where possible, a diagnosis fee that applies to the fix, and no work started without your yes.

items.title: Tune-up, mechanical
items.body: Every machine that sews forward and back. Includes bobbin case polish.

items.title: Tune-up, computerized
items.body: Same bench work, plus error-code history and firmware check.

items.title: Sergers
items.body: Loopers, knives, and the rethreading lesson you have been avoiding.

items.title: Walking foot service
items.body: Clean and re-grease. Bring it with the machine and the price is halved.

items.title: Scissors and rotary blades
items.body: Sharpened while you wait on Saturdays.

sections.heading: What to bring
sections.html:
The machine, its foot pedal and cords, one bobbin, and a story about what it is doing or refusing to do. If it is a repair, a photo of the stitch on scrap helps and so does the needle you were using.

Serger owners: thread it before you come if it will run at all. We can decode a threaded serger; an unthreaded one is a museum piece until you find the manual.

items.q: How long does a tune-up take?
items.a: Three to five shop days. Repairs depend on parts, and we call with the estimate before anything is ordered.
Everything mechanical and most computerized machines. For a few newer electronic models the maker holds the parts hostage, and we will tell you that up front.

items.q: Is the diagnosis fee really applied?
items.a: Yes, same day. If you decline the repair it covers the bench time, and the machine comes home reassembled and honest about what is wrong.

sections.title: Vintage restorations
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Blackside Singers, featherweights with original cases, and treadle cabinets that outlived three kitchens.

sections.heading: Kept running, not restored to death
sections.html:
The rule on this bench is to keep the machine the machine. Original decals stay, worn gold fill is left alone, and replacements are period-correct or clearly marked. A machine that sewed a wedding trousseau in 1938 should still look like it did.

Wiring is the exception. Cloth insulation fails and we rewire for safety, every time, before the machine goes home to a table where people sew.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: A workbench in a garage that grew a shop, twenty-two years of machines, and a parts drawer organized by decade.

sections.html:
The first machine on this bench was my grandmother's, brought back to life so she could finish a quilt for my graduation. The second and third belonged to neighbors. The hundredth was a brand that no longer exists, and the shop opened not long after, in a garage with good light and a concrete floor that forgives dropped presser feet.

We service what we sell, refurbish what we can, and tell you the truth about the rest. No appointment needed to drop off, though Saturdays fill by nine.

items.quote: The only shop I have ever trusted to touch my grandmother's machine, and now the only one that touches mine.
items.author: L., Kettering

sections.title: Book a repair
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Tell us the brand, the age, and what it is doing or refusing to do. We reply with the earliest bench slot.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.html: You get a confirmation with a drop-off window. At the bench the machine gets the diagnosis first, then a call with the number before any part is ordered. Most repairs that start on Monday are sewing again by Friday.
